items: Imagine a Bank class with a constructor that takes three arguments (bankName, area, and phoneNumber) that have the same names as the instance variables.
Without the this keyword, it would be unclear whether you're referring to the constructor parameters or the instance variables.
this.bankName refers to the instance variable, while bankName refers to the local variable (constructor parameter).
The this keyword resolves this ambiguity.
Accessing Instance Variables: If the names of instance variables and method parameters are the same, use this to differentiate them.
Invoking Other Constructors: You can use this() to call another constructor from the current one.
Passing the Current Object: this can be passed to another method or constructor to refer to the current object.

content.text: Objective: To understand the use of this keyword in Java.

items: Create the Bank class and save it as Bank.java.
Observe the use of this keyword when referring to instance variables in constructors or methods.
The this keyword is essential for clarity when local variables or parameters have the same name as instance variables.
It helps differentiate between the current object's instance variable and the method's parameter.
It can also be used to pass the current object (this) as an argument to other methods or constructors.
